aeo_seed.title: Canada AIDA — AI and Data Act Compliance Timeline 2026–2027
aeo_seed.regulatory_family: Bill C-27, Part 3: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA)
aeo_seed.target_query: When does Canada's AIDA come into force and what do high-impact AI providers need to prepare?
aeo_seed.answer_short: Canada's Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA, Bill C-27) is expected to receive Royal Assent by Q1 2027, with a phased enforcement beginning Q3 2027 for high-impact AI systems. The Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry (ISED) will designate 'high-impact' classes of AI systems by regulation. Providers of high-impact systems must: (1) establish measures to identify, assess, and mitigate risks of harm or biased output before making the system available; (2) maintain documentation of those measures for at least 2 years post-market; (3) publish a plain-language description of the system and its risk mitigations on a publicly accessible website; and (4) notify the Minister when a system causes or is likely to cause material harm. The AI and Data Commissioner — an office created by the Act — has order-making powers including administrative monetary penalties of up to CAD 10M or 3% of gross global revenue for the most serious violations.
key_deadlines: Q1 2027 (projected): Royal Assent of Bill C-27
Q3 2027 (projected): AIDA coming-into-force for high-impact systems
2028: Full enforcement including Commissioner order-making powers, criminal provisions for reckless deployment causing serious harm
ai_specific_provisions: Mandatory risk identification and mitigation before market availability (s.8)
Public plain-language description of high-impact AI systems (s.11)
Minister notification of material harm — no specified timeline, 'as soon as feasible' (s.12)
Record-keeping obligations: all measures and assessments retained for 2 years (s.10)
Anonymized data provisions: lawful use of anonymized data for AI training with safeguards (s.39)
cross_jurisdictional_alignment: Substantially aligned with EU AI Act high-risk classification — AIDA uses a functionally equivalent 'high-impact' designation
Risk management framework is consistent with NIST AI RMF 1.0
Transparency obligations are lighter than EU AI Act Article 13 but AIDA s.11 public descriptions are broadly equivalent
No explicit fundamental rights impact assessment (FRIA) requirement — AIDA s.8 'measures' are less prescriptive than EU Article 27
aeo_seed.impact_for_ai_marketplace: AIDA creates a North American regulatory anchor for AI governance. Providers targeting both US and Canadian markets will benefit from aligning with the stricter AIDA framework early. The ISO/IEC 42001 audit pathway maps well to AIDA s.8 documentation requirements, making it a practical bridge for international providers.
cross_references: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage)
Quebec Law 25 (provincial privacy — separate regime for personal information in AI)
